headline: Germany turned east in June, Japan struck Pearl Harbor in December, and Citizen Kane opened in May
texture: Operation Barbarossa opened in June and German forces reached the Dnieper by July. Einsatzgruppen units followed the army east and began mass shootings behind the front, and 23,600 Jews were killed at Kamianets-Podilskyi on August 27 alone. Roosevelt and Churchill met aboard ship on August 9. Britain declared war on Finland, Hungary and Romania on December 5.

Japanese carrier aircraft attacked Pearl Harbor and the Japanese declaration of war on the United States and the British Empire was published the same day. Hitler issued the Nacht und Nebel decree in December, under which political prisoners disappeared without record. The Lend-Lease Act had been introduced in Congress in January and passed the House on February 8.

Citizen Kane premiered in New York in May, Orson Welles's first film, and finished nowhere near the top of the box office. Sergeant York took nearly twice what the second-place film did, with Gary Cooper as a pacifist who becomes a war hero. How Green Was My Valley was fourth and won Best Picture. Glenn Miller's Chattanooga Choo Choo was the best-selling record. James Joyce died in January.

notes: Research pass July 2026. Barbarossa, the Nacht und Nebel decree and the Citizen Kane premiere carry months rather than days because the source lists them under month headings without days. Gary Cooper's role in Sergeant York, and Citizen Kane being nominated without winning, are general knowledge of those films rather than claims from the year pages.
